modeDescriptions.preCall: Before LLM Call - Runs before the LLM call and checks the input (Recommended)
modeDescriptions.duringCall: During LLM Call - Runs in parallel with the LLM call, with response held until check completes
modeDescriptions.postCall: After LLM Call - Runs after the LLM call and checks only the output
modeDescriptions.loggingOnly: Logging Only - Only runs on logging callbacks without affecting the LLM call
modeDescriptions.preMcpCall: Before MCP Tool Call - Runs before MCP tool execution and validates tool calls
modeDescriptions.duringMcpCall: During MCP Tool Call - Runs in parallel with MCP tool execution for monitoring
modeDescriptions.postMcpCall: After MCP Tool Call - Runs after MCP tool execution and checks the tool result

endpoint.description: Configure settings for a specific call type. Most guardrails don't need this — skip it unless you're using a specific endpoint like /v1/realtime.

endpoint.warnHint: Bot speaks the message, session continues
endpoint.endSessionHint: Bot speaks the message, connection closes immediately
endpoint.violationMessageHint: What the bot says aloud when this guardrail fires. Falls back to the default violation message if empty.

competitorIntent.title: Competitor Intent Filter
competitorIntent.offDescription: Block or reframe competitor comparison questions. When enabled, airline type auto-loads competitors from IATA; generic type requires manual competitor list.
competitorIntent.onDescription: Block or reframe competitor comparison questions. Airline type uses major airlines (excluding your brand); generic requires manual competitor list.
competitorIntent.brandSelfAirlinePlaceholder: Search or select airline, or type to add custom
competitorIntent.typeToAdd: Type and press Enter to add
competitorIntent.brandSelfAirlineHint: Select your airline from the list (excluded from competitors) or type to add a custom term
competitorIntent.brandSelfGenericHint: Names/codes users use for your brand
competitorIntent.locationsHint: Countries, cities, airports for disambiguation (e.g. qatar, doha)
competitorIntent.competitorsHint: Competitor names to detect (required for generic type)
competitorIntent.thresholdsIntro: Classify competitor intent by confidence (0–1). Higher confidence -> stronger intent.
competitorIntent.highHint: : Treat as full competitor comparison -> uses "Competitor comparison" policy
competitorIntent.mediumHint: : Treat as possible comparison -> uses "Possible competitor comparison" policy
competitorIntent.lowHint: : Log only; allow request. Below Low -> allow with no action
competitorIntent.thresholdsFooter: Raise thresholds to be more permissive; lower them to be stricter.

llmJudge.intro: After each LLM response, the Judge Model scores it 0–100 against your criteria. If the weighted average falls below the threshold, the response is blocked (or logged).
llmJudge.judgeModelHint: The LLM that reads each response and grades it. Pick a capable model — it never sees end-user data beyond what the LLM returned.
llmJudge.minScoreHint: 0–100. If the weighted average of criterion scores falls below this, the guardrail triggers. 80 is a good default.
llmJudge.onFailureHint: Block: return HTTP 422 when the score is too low. Log: record the result but let the response through.
llmJudge.criteriaHint: Each criterion is something the judge checks. Weights must add up to 100%.
llmJudge.weightHint: How much this criterion counts toward the final score. All weights must add up to 100%.
llmJudge.criterionDescriptionPlaceholder: What should the judge check for this criterion?

toolPermission.title: LiteLLM Tool Permission Guardrail
toolPermission.description: Provide regex patterns (e.g., ^mcp__github_.*$) for tool names or types and optionally constrain payload fields.
toolPermission.onDisallowedHint: Block returns an error when a forbidden tool is invoked. Rewrite strips the tool call but lets the rest of the response continue.
